concept_html:
Nine snippets of PySpark and Spark SQL, each with one seeded bug. Most come straight from your reference pipeline's known defects. The answer key stays hidden until you submit.

Use the same routine as lesson D7-L1: read the goal, walk the lines, ask what each line assumes. Spark adds its own questions:

  • Imports. Is sum, min, max, round or filter imported by name from pyspark.sql.functions? Is functions as F used instead?
  • Filters. Does a comparison with a nullable column drop nulls? Is a boolean compared with == True?
  • Grain. Does every groupBy include each grain column the docstring names? Does every join keep the grain?
  • Aggregates. Can a sum(when(...)) return null? Is a division guarded?
  • Passes over the data. Are there several count() calls on an uncached DataFrame, where one agg would do?
  • Writes. Does a MERGE source hold one row per key? Is a rename silently skipped when the source column is missing?
  • SQL. Does NOT IN meet a nullable subquery?

For each snippet, tap the line, then write the fix. The checker tests the fix statically: it looks for the pattern the standard requires. Your score counts bugs found and fixes proposed.

When you finish, compare your list of misses with the checklist above. The item you missed most is the one to add to your personal review routine.

title: Review practice: PySpark and Spark SQL
why_html: Spark code fails quietly more often than Python code. A shadowed import fails loudly. A missing grain column, a null sum or a duplicate MERGE key can pass every run and still publish wrong numbers. Practice on the defects from your own pipeline trains your eye for the ones that will appear in its next version.
